parts.title: January 2026
parts.html:
Khelo India on sand and snow

  • 2nd Khelo India Beach Games: 5–10 January at Ghoghla Beach, Diu; mascot 'Pearl' the dolphin; 8 disciplines (6 medal, 2 demo); Karnataka topped the table.
  • 6th Khelo India Winter Games: 20–26 January at Leh (ice sports) and Gulmarg (snow sports); mascot 'Shan' the snow leopard; figure skating added for the first time.

Tennis and badminton

  • Australian Open 2026: Carlos Alcaraz (men's singles) and Elena Rybakina (women's singles).
  • Brisbane International: Daniil Medvedev and Aryna Sabalenka (her third Brisbane title).
  • India Open (New Delhi): Lin Chun-Yi (men) and An Se-young (women); An Se-young also won the Malaysia Open.
  • India's Devika Sihag won the Thailand Masters women's singles – her first BWF Super 300 title.
  • Saina Nehwal retired; her 2012 London bronze was India's first Olympic badminton medal, and she was world No. 1 in 2015.
  • Venus Williams, 47, became the oldest player at the Australian Open.

Cricket

  • Vidarbha won the Vijay Hazare Trophy for the first time, beating Saurashtra in Bengaluru; Aman Mokhade top scorer (814 runs).
  • Australia won the Ashes 2025-26 4–1; Mitchell Starc player of the series.
  • New Zealand won the ODI series in India 2–1; India won the T20I series 4–1 (Suryakumar Yadav player of series).
  • India U-19 swept South Africa 3–0; Vaibhav Suryavanshi player of series.
  • Virat Kohli (28,068 international runs) passed Kumar Sangakkara and is second only to Sachin Tendulkar.
  • Nat Sciver-Brunt scored the first-ever WPL century.
  • Scotland replaced Bangladesh in the T20 World Cup 2026 (India and Sri Lanka, from 7 February).
  • Australia captain Alyssa Healy will retire after the India series.

Hockey and football

  • Women's Hockey India League: SG Pipers champions (final at Ranchi, captain Navneet Kaur); men's HIL: Vedanta Kalinga Lancers (Bhubaneswar).
  • Sjoerd Marijne returns as chief coach of the Indian women's hockey team.
  • Amelia Valverde (Costa Rica) appointed coach of the Indian women's football team.
  • Hyderabad will host the women's FIH World Cup qualifier (8–14 March 2026).
  • The FIFA World Cup 2026 trophy toured India; the Cup (USA, Canada, Mexico) has 48 teams for the first time.

National championships

  • Senior National Boxing, Greater Noida – first combined men's and women's event by BFI; Nikhat Zareen (52 kg) and Lovlina Borgohain (75 kg) won.
  • National Volleyball, Varanasi: Railways (men) and Kerala (women).
  • Pro Wrestling League returned after 7 years; Haryana Thunders won.
  • Senior National Kho-Kho, Kazipet: RSPB (men), Maharashtra (women).
  • Tata Steel Chess India, Kolkata: Nihal Sarin won open rapid; Wesley So won open blitz.
  • Aaryan Varshney became India's 92nd Grandmaster.
  • Atiqa Mir, 11, became the first female to finish top-5 in the IAME UAE karting championship.

Rules and bodies

  • National Sports Governance (National Sports Bodies) Rules, 2026 notified under the 2025 Act: at least four 'Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit' in each general body, half of them women.
  • A task force led by Pullela Gopichand suggested a National Coach Accreditation Board and 'TOPS for Coaches'.
  • Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani (Qatar) elected President of the Olympic Council of Asia.
  • Deaths: Davinder Singh Garcha (1980 Moscow Olympic hockey gold), Manoj Kothari (1990 world billiards champion), ex-BCCI chief I.S. Bindra, coach Michael Nobbs.
